title: Permissions

A layer declares **capabilities**. One backend layer registers a **permissions driver** that loads the capability list of the current user. Core reads that list to decide what the admin shows.

## Declare a capability

```ts [app/plugins/pluto-registrations.ts]
export default defineNuxtPlugin(() => {
  definePlutoExtension({
    id: 'supabase-blog',
    capabilities: [
      {
        id: 'posts-publish',
        key: 'posts:publish',
        label: 'Publish posts',
        description: 'Change a post from draft to published.'
      }
    ]
  })
})
```

A capability key has the format `<namespace>:<action>`, lowercase. Examples: `posts:publish`, `settings:manage`.

::note
A setting key is a different string. It uses a dot, for example `blog.posts_per_page`. Do not mix the two formats.
::

### `key` and `id`

A capability has both an `id` and a `key`. They hold different strings on purpose.

- `id` identifies the registry entry. The registry rewrites it to `<extensionId>:<id>`.
- `key` is the capability string. The registry never changes it.

Use a plain `id` such as `posts-publish`. Put the real string in `key`.

## `usePlutoCapabilities()`

```ts
const { items, groups, groupsFor } = usePlutoCapabilities()
```

`items` lists every declared capability. The list is for documentation and typing. The database stores capability strings as free text. A capability works even if no layer declares it.

`groups` groups the capabilities by owner, for a picker such as the Roles editor. A layer names its group with the locale key `<owner>.capabilities.group`. `groupsFor(keys)` adds an "Other" group for strings that no layer declares.

## `usePlutoPermissions()`

```ts
const { granted, loaded, status, hasDriver, isAdmin, load, ensureLoaded, clear, can } = usePlutoPermissions()

await ensureLoaded(user.id)
can('posts:publish')
```

| Member | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `granted` | The capability strings that the driver returned |
| `loaded` | `true` after `load()` completed once |
| `status` | `'idle'` or `'loading'` |
| `hasDriver` | `true` when a layer registered a permissions driver |
| `isAdmin` | `true` when `granted` includes `*` |
| `load(userId?)` | Calls the driver. One request runs at a time. |
| `ensureLoaded(userId)` | Returns at once when the list is loaded for this user. It rejects when the driver rejects. |
| `clear()` | Resets the state. Core calls it on sign-out. |
| `can(capability)` | `true` if the user holds the capability or `*` |

::warning
`can()` fails **open** when no permissions driver is registered. A site with no permissions backend has no server-side guard, so hiding UI would give no protection. Check `hasDriver` if you need to tell the two cases apart.
::

::warning
`can()` is a UI convenience. It is never a security boundary. A user can call your API directly. The real enforcement is the server-side guard of the backend layer, backed by row-level security.
::

## Staff-only admin

Core uses the capability list in two places:

- The plugin `pluto-auth-sync.client.ts` loads the list on sign-in and clears it on sign-out. It also syncs the admin language.
- The route guard waits for the list. A signed-in user with no capability goes to `/admin/no-access`.

See [Admin shell](/core/admin-shell).

## Limits

- Core has no roles UI. The supabase layer adds one. See [Users and roles](/supabase/users-and-roles).
- There are no capability hierarchies and no namespace wildcards. The only wildcard is `*`.
- A permissions driver for an admin must return `['*']`. If it returns `[]`, the admin is locked out of the admin pages.
